What Is a Mutual Action Plan?

Explainerlowob research

By lowob · 22 October 2026 · 5-minute read · Revenue

A mutual action plan (MAP) is a shared document, agreed by buyer and seller, that lists the steps to a purchase decision and the start of work, each with a date and a named owner. It turns a close date the seller hopes for into a sequence the buyer has accepted. A plan the buyer never confirmed is a forecast assumption, not a mutual plan.

What a mutual action plan means

Deals often slip on steps nobody listed: a security review, a legal redline, a budget sign-off in another department. A MAP lists those steps in advance, in the buyer's order, each assigned to a person on one side or the other.

Outreach account executive Ryan Jander, in a 2021 company blog, calls it "a shared document that helps a buyer and seller collaborate on a shared buying process". His contents list includes a value summary, go-live dates, milestones, deadlines, an owner and outcomes. Aviso's product documentation calls it "a collaborative workspace designed to align buyers and sellers on key milestones", with buyer and seller roles and a due date on each action item.

A mutual action plan isIt is not
Agreed with the buyer and visible to themAn internal close plan the buyer never sees
A list of buyer and seller steps, each with an ownerA list of the seller's tasks only
Dated backwards from the buyer's go-live or decision dateDated forwards from the seller's quarter end
Updated as steps move, with changes keptRewritten so it always looks on track

Why it matters for a commercial team

Buying decisions are not linear. Gartner's buyer enablement research describes a typical buying group of six to ten stakeholders and six "buying jobs": problem identification, solution exploration, requirements building, supplier selection, validation and consensus creation. Gartner also found that 95% of buying groups go back to revisit decisions at least once as new information emerges. A plan must be able to record those loops.

Consensus is where deals stall. In a May 2025 release, Gartner reported that 74% of buyer teams in a survey of 632 B2B buyers showed "unhealthy conflict". Groups that reached consensus were 2.5 times more likely to report a high-quality deal. A MAP does not create consensus, but it shows which members of the buying committee have taken part and which steps wait on them.

It also tests the forecast. A deal in Commit needs evidence, as set out in What Is a Forecast Category?. Buyer procurement and legal steps dated inside the quarter are that evidence; blank steps are a warning.

In lowob's model, the MAP is a shared record of commitments, and each change is a small decision. When the buyer moves the security review back two weeks, the plan should show the old date, the new date and the reason. Some tools sync the plan into the CRM; Trumpet's help pages say its MAP on the HubSpot deal record "stays in sync". The reasons for changes still need recording. Supersede, Never Overwrite applies to dates as much as to prices.

How to build one

An illustrative MAP for a services engagement, dated backwards from the buyer's start date:

StepOwnerSideDueEvidence it is done
Confirm problem and success measuresHead of operationsBuyerWeek 1Written success measures
Scoping workshopAccount leadSellerWeek 2Agreed scope note
Proposal and pricingAccount leadSellerWeek 3Proposal sent
Security and data reviewIT leadBuyerWeek 5Questionnaire returned
Commercial and legal termsProcurement and counselBuyerWeek 6Redlines closed
Budget approvalFinance directorBuyerWeek 7Purchase order raised
Signature and kick-off dateEconomic buyerBuyerWeek 8Signed contract

Write it with the buyer, not for them, working back from their decision date. Put buyer steps first, since sellers cannot control them. Review it at every meeting and record each date change with its reason.

Agents can draft the first version from past deals of the same type. Under lowob's Gateway 1, the draft goes to the account lead before the client sees it, because a MAP sent in error commits the firm to dates the client never agreed.

lowob takeaways

  • Mutual means the buyer agreed. A plan the buyer has not confirmed is an assumption.
  • List buyer steps first. Security, legal and budget approvals are where deals slip.
  • Keep the changes. Every moved date is a small decision with a reason.

Sources and notes

  • Aviso documentation, Mutual Action Plan, undated. Vendor product documentation, cited as a category example.
  • Trumpet Help Center, View and update mutual action plans in HubSpot, undated. Vendor product documentation, cited for CRM sync only.
  • Gartner, Buyer Enablement, undated. Analyst research summary; survey of more than 250 B2B customers, no date given.
  • Gartner, Sales Survey Finds 74% of B2B Buyer Teams Demonstrate "Unhealthy Conflict", 7 May 2025. Analyst press release; 632 buyers surveyed August to September 2024.

Next move

Pick one late-stage deal and list every step left before signature. Mark which are buyer steps with no named buyer owner, and ask the buyer to fill those names at your next meeting.
